thesisQuality.note: Strong durable fleet-renewal demand, 6,200+ aircraft backlog and material lessor order support the strong band; incomplete economic conversion prevents exceptional treatment.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Deliveries and production improved, but negative 2.7% Commercial Airplanes margin, negative first-half FCF and high debt keep momentum mixed/unproven.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: September market capitalization around $166B against still-weak realized cash/margins makes valuation demanding rather than clearly asymmetric; execution upside exists but is not yet proven.

catalystScore.note: 737 rate transition, completed -7/-10 certification flight testing and expected certification/deliveries provide identifiable catalysts, tempered by execution timing risk.

governancePower.note: Liquidity/debt actions and improving production are constructive, but program losses, safety/quality history embedded in execution risk and incomplete profitability keep governance/execution evidence mixed.

alignment2036.note: Large-scale commercial aviation, defense and aerospace capacity serve durable mobility and infrastructure needs across plausible 2036 futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Commercial airplanes, defense/space and services provide multiple demand engines using shared aerospace engineering/manufacturing capabilities, though program economics vary.

bottleneckControl.note: Certified large-aircraft supply is concentrated, backlog is massive and qualification/capacity lead times are long; Airbus prevents monopoly-level scoring.

scenarioRobustness.note: Diversified aerospace exposure and backlog support resilience, but debt, regulatory/certification and supplier execution create meaningful scenario dependence.

substitutionResilience.note: Aircraft qualification, installed fleets and OEM scale create high replacement friction, while Airbus and future architectures remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Production-rate progress shows functioning throughput, but supplier stability remains a binding conversion constraint and redundancy is not sufficiently evidenced for a strong band.

pricingPower.note: Scarce certified-aircraft capacity and backlog imply some pricing leverage, but negative Commercial Airplanes margin shows value capture is not yet durably demonstrated.

riskEvidence.note: Material execution, certification, supplier, leverage and cash-conversion risks persist despite strong demand and improving throughput.

dataConfidenceEvidence.note: Core operating and demand facts are primary-source addressed and valuation has independent market evidence; normalized future economics and broader independent corroboration remain uncertain.

scoreRecord.thesis: Boeing controls one of the world's scarce certified large-aircraft platforms with deep backlog and improving throughput, but value realization depends on restoring durable margins, cash conversion, quality execution and balance-sheet resilience.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Operational/certification or supplier setbacks could prevent backlog from converting into profitable deliveries while leverage limits downside tolerance.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: 737 production-rate progression plus 737-7/-10 certification and first-delivery milestones.
